page: Amazon Web Services m6a.large is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz, structured with 1 physical CPU core supporting 2 vCPUs via multithreading. System memory totals 8.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard general-purpose resource ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 4 MB of L3 cache per core. Hardware security and execution features include AES, VAES, SHA-NI, AVX, BMI2, and IBRS. The instance provides 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no local instance storage, and includes no discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluation reveals distinct performance characteristics across single-threaded and multi-core workloads. Single-core performance tests via stress-ng place the instance in the top 25% of evaluated cloud systems, complemented by solid single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression metrics. However, multi-core CPU efficiency and overall memory bandwidth measure in lower percentiles, with uncached read memory bandwidth reaching 31.17 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaching 21.04 GB/sec. Synthetic benchmarks such as Geekbench and PassMark reflect lower multi-core output, software compilation throughput, and database transaction rates, primarily due to the single physical core layout shared across two execution threads.

From a qualitative resource balance perspective, the instance delivers predictable, dedicated compute execution without burstable CPU credit constraints. Eliminating bundled local NVMe storage lowers hardware resource overhead for deployments relying on network-attached storage. The technical profile offers efficient utilization for small-scale web serving, light text processing services, single-threaded background jobs, microservices, and general entry-level backend tasks where high memory throughput or heavy multi-threaded compute is not required.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.large is a general-purpose instance powered by a 3.6 GHz AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs via hyperthreading on an x86_64 architecture. Managed by the AWS Nitro System, it provides dedicated CPU allocation alongside 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance includes 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and relies entirely on external block storage, featuring no local NVMe drives or discrete GPU acceleration. Benchmark testing demonstrates strong single-core CPU output, though multi-core execution and overall memory bandwidth fall into lower performance percentiles. Text processing, gzip compression, and small-model LLM text generation achieve average throughput rates, whereas database operations and code compilation show modest results. This resource profile provides qualitative cost efficiency for general lightweight services, small-scale web servers, basic background tasks, and low-concurrency application backends.
